_comment: Single source of truth for the Docker Scout 'clean bill of health' image set. Every image under `required` must earn a grade-A Docker Scout health score. CI enforces this in two places, both driven by this file (via the scout-config job): (1) PR time, .github/workflows/build.yml gates the policies that are deterministically checkable on a locally-built image -- fixable CRITICAL/HIGH CVEs (via scripts/scout-cve-gate.sh) and the default-non-root-user policy; (2) release time, .github/workflows/publish.yml runs scripts/scout-grade.sh on the PUSHED image, which is the only place the full grade can be checked because supply-chain attestations (15 pts), base images and the SBOM exist only on push. scout-grade.sh checks the health-score rules itself, because `docker scout policy` is an org-level call the OIDC login cannot make (#150). `cve_net_extra` lists extra builder images that get the fixable CRITICAL/HIGH CVE net only, NOT the full grade-A bill of health. A required image may WAIVE a specific fixable finding it has assessed as not exploitable by adding an OpenVEX `not_affected` statement under .github/vex/ (scoped to the image + CVE); the PR gate (scout-cve-gate.sh) lists findings and drops VEX-waived ones, fail-closed -- an auditable, standards-based assessment, not a silent allowlist. `exempt` lists images deliberately left OUT of the grade-A set with a documented reason -- each fails ONLY on third-party-bundled, upstream-frozen CVEs whose vulnerable code IS in the image's execute path (so a VEX not_affected would be false), and which buildenv cannot patch in place. The non-root audit still reports exempt images; they are simply not hard-gated. Exempt-image remediations and active VEX waivers (with their drop triggers) are tracked in docs/upstream-cve-backlog.md. To require a new service, add it to `required` (and add the matching non-root USER + clean deps first). See README 'Image security policies'.

exempt.build-e2e: Assembly image: COPYs already-published third-party release artifacts (martin/shirotester/pdfserv Go binaries, newman's npm deps, wkhtmltopdf's patched-Qt .deb) carrying ~70 fixable CRITICAL/HIGH CVEs buildenv cannot patch without upstream rebuilds. The vulnerable code runs (these are executed tools/binaries), so VEX not_affected does not apply. Grade A is unreachable regardless of base hygiene; keeps its root default (a non-root flip earned no payoff). Upstream backlog: docs/upstream-cve-backlog.md.
exempt.build-js: azure-cli's vendored Python deps carry 2 fixable HIGH (pyjwt 2.12.0 -> 2.13.0 CVE-2026-48526; cryptography 46.0.7 -> 48.0.1 GHSA-537c-gmf6-5ccf). az actually uses these libs (vulnerable code is in the execute path -> not a VEX not_affected case). No buildenv lever: azure-cli 2.87.0 is already the latest release and still bundles the vulnerable versions; Microsoft must bump them. The big golang/stdlib cluster (was 4C + ~25H, from Debian's EOL-Go git-lfs) IS fixed here (official git-lfs binary). Stays non-root. Re-promote when a newer azure-cli ships patched deps. Upstream backlog: docs/upstream-cve-backlog.md.
exempt.build-swaggercodegen: All residual CVEs (1 CRITICAL + 16 HIGH) live inside the third-party swagger-codegen-cli-v3:3.0.34 JAR (snakeyaml, jackson-core, logback, commons-beanutils, commons-io, handlebars) -- libraries the codegen tool actually runs (execute path -> not a VEX not_affected case). buildenv only COPYs the jar; the fixed versions (e.g. commons-beanutils 1.11.0, handlebars 4.5.2) are too recent for the swagger-codegen 3.0.x line to have adopted, so even the latest 3.0.x jar would not fully clear them. Stays non-root. Re-promote if/when a swagger-codegen jar ships clean deps. Upstream backlog: docs/upstream-cve-backlog.md.
exempt.awscli: Thin wrapper of Amazon's amazon/aws-cli image (pinned AWSCLI_VER) that only runs the build-harden kit (images/harden), which removes the eMudhra emSign roots and blocks the leaked intermediates. The CLI, its Python and Amazon Linux packages are Amazon's build; buildenv changes only the trust store, so any CVE is fixed by bumping AWSCLI_VER to a newer Amazon release. Keeps the upstream root user, which the mars init containers rely on.
exempt.dind: Wrapper of docker:<DIND_VERSION>-dind (Docker 28.5.2, the last 28 release: Fabric 2.5's peer cannot build chaincode on Docker 29, see images/Dockerfile.dind) that removes the eMudhra emSign roots, upgrades the Alpine packages and adds an entrypoint that clears a legacy BuildKit cache. Its remaining fixable CRITICAL/HIGH CVEs are Go modules built into Docker's own binaries (golang.org/x/net < 0.60.0, github.com/moby/go-archive < 0.3.0), which run (execute path, so VEX not_affected does not apply) and which only a newer Docker release clears. Runs privileged as root by design (Docker-in-Docker).
exempt.fabric-tools: Thin wrapper of hyperledger/fabric-tools (pinned FABRIC_TOOLS_VERSION) that only removes the eMudhra emSign roots, as the ko base image of luthersystems/fabric-snapshot-archiver. Its Ubuntu packages and Fabric binaries are upstream builds; buildenv changes only the trust store. Keeps the upstream root user, which the peer CLI and the peer-volume mount rely on.
exempt.fabric-baseos: Thin wrapper of hyperledger/fabric-baseos (Fabric 2.2 and 2.4, pinned FABRIC_2_2_VERSION and FABRIC_2_4_VERSION; tags 2.2 and 2.4), the image a peer runs Docker chaincode in, that only runs the build-harden kit. Fabric no longer releases 2.2 or 2.4, so their Alpine packages are frozen upstream; buildenv changes only the trust store. Keeps the upstream chaincode user.
exempt.fabric-ccenv: Thin wrapper of hyperledger/fabric-ccenv (Fabric 2.2, 2.4 and 2.5, pinned FABRIC_<minor>_VERSION; tags 2.2, 2.4 and 2.5), the image a peer builds Docker chaincode in, that only runs the build-harden kit. Its packages and Go toolchain are upstream builds that the chaincode build depends on, so buildenv changes only the trust store. Keeps the upstream chaincode user.
exempt.build-harden: The build-harden kit (images/harden): a FROM scratch image of shell scripts and policy data, never run as a container. Repos bind-mount it into their own builds. It has no packages, so there is no CVE to fix, and it holds the listed CA certificates on purpose (they are the policy). scripts/ci-harden-check.sh checks that it holds exactly the committed kit.
